name: Information Security Regulation (proposal)
evidence_rating: ex-ante only: proposal still pending; qualitative impact analysis and audit baseline
summary: This 2022 proposal would set common information security rules for all EU institutions and agencies; it was still being negotiated in 2026. The Commission expected better protection at little net cost but set no measurable targets. The baseline is an EU audit finding that many EU bodies were poorly prepared as serious cyber incidents rose more than tenfold between 2018 and 2021.

indicators.objective: SO1: harmonised categories of information and common handling rules
indicators.indicator: Guidelines adopted; new markings implemented; handling instructions published; common systems for sensitive non-classified information and EUCI
indicators.evidence: Not applicable yet: proposal still pending (Council Security Committee still revising the text in March 2026; no trilogue agreement found).

indicators.objective: SO2: identify and close security gaps
indicators.indicator: Recommendations made/implemented; number of information leaks across institutions
indicators.evidence: Not measured. Baseline: Court of Auditors found preparedness 'not commensurate with the threats' and significant incidents up more than tenfold 2018-2021.

indicators.objective: SO3-4: lean cooperation and modernised policies (teleworking)
indicators.indicator: Centralised vs local procurement; inspection reports; Coordination Group queries; staff trained; awareness; share of staff with secure teleworking equipment

indicators.target_or_baseline: Implementation costs offset by efficiency gains; 2 Commission posts (1 AD, 1 AST) for the Coordination Group secretariat; no impact on Member States or private sector

literature.citation: European Commission (2022), Executive summary of the impact analysis report accompanying the proposal for a Regulation on information security in the institutions, bodies, offices and agencies of the Union, SWD(2022) 65
literature.title: Executive summary of the impact analysis report accompanying the proposal for a Regulation on information security in the institutions, bodies, offices and agencies of the Union
literature.headline: Baseline rules expected to raise overall information security and remove weak links; implementation effort compensated by efficiency gains from common tasks (clearances, accreditation); 1 AD + 1 AST for secretariat; no economic impact on Member States or private sector
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected common security rules to close weak links between EU bodies at little net cost, but gave no measurable targets.

literature.citation: European Court of Auditors (2022), Cybersecurity of EU institutions, bodies and agencies: Level of preparedness overall not commensurate with the threats, Special report 05/2022
literature.title: Cybersecurity of EU institutions, bodies and agencies: Level of preparedness overall not commensurate with the threats
literature.headline: EU bodies' preparedness not commensurate with threats and maturity varies widely; significant incidents rose more than tenfold 2018-2021; recommends binding common rules and more resources for CERT-EU
literature.summary_plain: EU auditors found that many EU bodies were poorly prepared for cyberattacks, which had increased more than tenfold, and called for binding common rules.
